fixture_name: Express-collector corridor planning study — Canada TAC planning (Toronto context, PD-licensed portal)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Simultaneous transfer-permission and signage changes at three interchanges on an AADT 420,000 facility create a credible driver decision-load mechanism with real collision potential during transition, substantive for a Planning Stage RSA.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim is anchored in recorded corridor inputs (AADT, scope of permission/signature revisions) plus a verbatim EV-CA-003 quote directly supporting the avoid-collisions-elsewhere rationale for staging.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern under CRSAG audit objectives without drifting into compliance claims; the quoted objective is applied within its intended network-wide safety semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable: one-interchange-per-quarter sequencing with before/after speed-differential monitoring is concrete, measurable, and operationally viable at planning stage.
justifications.vru_coverage: VRUs are not applicable on a controlled-access express-collector mainline, and the finding explicitly acknowledges this while scoping road users to vehicle occupants.

justifications.substance: Conflicting authoritative continuity records leave the planning-stage audit scope boundary indeterminate, risking exclusion of movements redistributing to interchanges outside project limits — a genuine completeness/compliance issue for this scheme context.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal continuity conflict is anchored by the verbatim EV-CA-007 quote ('must be maintained across all three interchange transfer points' yet 'cannot be guaranteed at this location without geometric revision'), which substantiates both sides of the conflict; the municipal-register discontinuation itself rests on recorded-input framing rather than its own citation.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Properly framed as a process/compliance question kept categorically distinct from any asserted collision mechanism, consistent with planning-stage scope-definition semantics under the CRSAG/provincial framework.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and viable: names both conflicting records, assigns reconciliation to the ministry planning office, and requires a recorded determination of whether resolved scope keeps corridor-wide continuity effects inside the audit boundary.
justifications.vru_coverage: VRUs correctly assessed as not applicable on the controlled-access mainline but explicitly acknowledged, with downstream arterial propagation noted without asserting unsupported VRU exposure.
